The result is faster narrowing of the arteries, which is what leads to heart attacks and strokes. The combined effect is larger than any single factor."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Can thin people have metabolic syndrome or fatty liver?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes, and it's common in India. Drug developers therefore created molecules that activate the same receptor but remain active for much longer."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"What was the importance of exenatide?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Exenatide was one of the first GLP-1 receptor agonists used clinically. Its development was influenced by research into exendin-4, a peptide discovered in the saliva of the Gila monster."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"What made semaglutide different?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Semaglutide was engineered to have a much longer duration of action than natural GLP-1, allowing once-weekly injection. Its development also helped establish the important role of GLP-1 therapy in chronic weight management."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Is tirzepatide a GLP-1 medicine?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Tirzepatide is more accurately described as a dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist because it acts on both receptors."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"What are triple agonists?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Triple agonists are medicines designed to activate three different hormonal pathways. Retatrutide is an investigational example that targets GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon receptors."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Are oral GLP-1 medicines available?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes. Oral GLP-1 treatment is now a real therapeutic approach. Oral semaglutide demonstrated that a GLP-1-based peptide medicine could be delivered by mouth, while newer small-molecule approaches are being developed for oral administration."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Will GLP-1 injections eventually disappear?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"There is no reason to assume that. Oral medicines are expanding the available options, but injectable and oral treatments have different characteristics and may suit different clinical situations."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Are newer GLP-1 medicines automatically better?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Not necessarily. A newer mechanism does not automatically mean that a medicine is more appropriate for a particular person. Treatment needs to be selected according to the patient's medical condition, goals, risks and the medicine's approved indication."}}]}]}
